plate.subject: a grey occupied city under pale lanterns

paragraphs.text: The Third Age began when Elzon conquered Aenor in 2A 2133 and ended with his permanent death, which let a human monarchy return. It lasted at least 1,200 years and many generations of men. By the reckoning of the scholars it lasted 1,260 years, and Elzon died in 3A 1260.
paragraphs.note: The length of at least 1,200 years, the start and the end are established; the 1,260 years and the year 3A 1260 are proposed.

sources.section: Working, proposed, or not fully specified

paragraphs.text: Volgan stayed in the Ember Lands, too weak to travel beyond them, and gave his orders to his servant Elzon, the Great Spirit and Great Necromancer. Elzon ruled Aenor in fact, but he had to use living servants, and he could never conquer the Magical Lands. Varner, a Lesser Spirit and wizard, and his small purple servant Golbran resisted the curses of the dead, and men all through Aenor refused to surrender entirely.

Elzon’s dead grew harder to keep as his reserves dwindled. The magic of Aenor would not renew him as the Ember Lands could, so he tried to change the land itself and make Aenor another Ember Lands. The elves, Varner and the stubborn resistance of men stood in his way. His decline was long, not sudden, and he held his dominion for centuries with changing armies and governors.

sources.section: Third Age rule and final death

paragraphs.text: No host of fading corpses could stand at full strength for twelve centuries. Elzon moved his hosts between the regions near his sources of power, raised new dead from each war, set living rulers over the provinces and leaned on orc and goblin garrisons. Some lands even kept an ordinary trade under heavy taxes. Rebels could be beaten without being wiped out, and so the wars came back in every generation, while both sides learned new ways to fight.

sources.section: Why the long rule holds together

paragraphs.text: At the end of the age Elzon died, and a catastrophe came with his death. The Deliverer saved the people from it and was proclaimed and worshipped as a New God. He did not take the throne. A good king of men restored Aenor, and the Fourth Age began. Varner and Golbran outlived the age.

plate.subject: a pale fortress above tribute roads

paragraphs.text: Elzon, the Great Spirit and Great Necromancer who served Volgan, seized Aenor in 2A 2133 and founded his own order, and the Third Age began. Volgan was too weak to leave the Ember Lands and sent his commands from there. Within Aenor, Elzon held the real power.

sources.section: Third Age rule and final death

paragraphs.text: The occupation lasted many generations, and no single generation of risen corpses could hold it. The dead fade, and raising them again uses magic that is hard to renew in Aenor. Elzon therefore ruled through living administrators, orc and goblin forces, fresh raisings of the dead, raids, lesser lords sworn to him, and arrangements that changed from province to province.

The Magical Lands were never conquered, and men rose against him again and again. Elzon tried to make Aenor able to sustain him as the Ember Lands did, but he never finished the work. He ruled until his literal and permanent death.

sources.section: Third Age rule and final death

paragraphs.text: Garrison towns, tribute roads and client rulers held the order together through the long centuries. Later historians call his rule the Pale Regency; what it called itself is not known.

The scholars divide the twelve centuries and more of the occupation into eight periods. In the first, the Order Takes Root (3A 1 to 180), Elzon’s living governors and his hosts of the dead secured the heart of Aenor, while the early revolts held out in forest and mountain strongholds.

In the Long Occupation proper (181 to 430) an uneasy order took hold. Garrison towns, tribute roads and client rulers made the conquest last for centuries, and resistance passed from father to son. In the Buried Wars (431 to 690), wars in the provinces and the Dark Lands wore down Elzon’s soldiers, and his necromancers refilled his hosts by robbing graves and renewing old bindings.

In the time of the Black Roots (691 to 910) Elzon hastened his work to corrupt the magic beneath Aenor, and his advance on the Magical Lands broke against the elves and Varner. In the Weakening Crown (911 to 1110) several regions won freedom for a time. Elzon could take them back, but each war cost him power he could not replace without Zol’s old magic.

In the Hidden Preparations (1111 to 1235) the counterspells of Varner and Golbran spread, charities grew among the poor, and rival groups made ready to break Elzon’s hold. The War of Unbinding (1236 to 1259) followed, and the age ended with the Last Tithe in 3A 1260.

plate.subject: elven wardens at a forest edge, the dead halted at the trees

paragraphs.text: The Magical Lands were never conquered. Through all the Third Age the elves, Varner the Lesser Spirit and Golbran resisted Elzon’s magic, and men went on fighting him in Aenor.

Varner is a wise wizard and a Lesser Spirit of the Magical Lands, in the form of an old man. He helped the elves and the resistance of men withstand Elzon’s necromancy through the long Third Age, for he can undo the curse that binds the risen dead. He has a small purple servant of unknown origin, Golbran. His wisdom stayed influential for centuries, yet his order remains that of a Lesser Spirit.

The elves of the Magical Lands fought to defend their own unconquered lands. That fitted their old refusal: no elven host marched to free the crown of men, though single travellers, healers and others worked across the races.
Varner is one wizard among many traditions of magic. He and Golbran outlived the Third Age.

plate.subject: black veins spreading beneath a burial field

paragraphs.text: The Black Roots were Elzon’s unfinished attempt to turn Aenor into a land that would sustain his necromancy as the Ember Lands did. They were a network of buried anchors, corrupted burial fields and places where the magic of life was turned inside out. Only in some places were they roots of any kind.

The work quickened between 3A 691 and 910. Elzon needed the Magical Lands, because their free and living magic kept his work from ever being complete, and his advance on them failed against the elves and Varner.
Varner and Golbran helped undo the links or cut them. The breaking of the network was one of the causes of Elzon’s final collapse.

sources.section: Third Age limitations and permanent death

paragraphs.text: The scholars do not agree where the first anchors were sunk.

The Lantern Chain was a network of resistance couriers, hidden refuges and keepers of wards, raised in the Third Age with the help of Varner and Golbran. Its purpose was to spread the ways of lifting the curse of the dead and to shield common folk from Elzon.

It worked beside the rebel bands of men. It never made the elven armies of the Magical Lands the official rescuers of Aenor. Its members carried the healing and farming learned in the Second Age, as well as rare magical wards.
Through its couriers the counterspells of Varner and Golbran reached far beyond the Magical Lands in the last centuries of the age.

The War of Unbinding was the last war of the resistance in the Third Age, fought to break the works that sustained Elzon’s army of the dead. It lasted from 3A 1236 to 1259 and ended in the Last Tithe.

Free armies of men, local rebels, friendly lesser rulers and defenders who stood with Varner and Golbran destroyed or unbound the necromantic anchors, above all those that let Elzon keep the dead near the capital. Varner freed many of those who were bound. Elzon’s power to keep his armies and to corrupt the magic of Aenor began to fail.

The elves of the Magical Lands held their own defences and sacred places, but the old kingdoms did not raise King Edran’s Grand Alliance again. The memory of the failed attack on the Ember Lands still shaped their choices.
Elzon’s hold depended more and more on Zol’s ancient magic, and that dependence prepared his destruction. Exactly how Zol consumed the Great Spirit is not known.

plate.subject: a black light collapsing over a capital

paragraphs.text: After more than twelve centuries of rule the Great Necromancer was exhausted. To steady his failing dominion and his army of the dead, Elzon drew on far more of Zol’s old magic than ever before. The resistance of men and the counterspells of Varner had already broken much of what held his power up.
paragraphs.note: The weakening by the resistance and Varner is established; the final overdraw is the proposed account.

sources.section: Third Age rule and final death

paragraphs.text: The bond turned against him. It did not merely banish his manifestation; it destroyed his spirit, and Elzon died, literally and for ever. Zol took his essence without stirring, and his strength grows in the far north still. The Old God did not take the field.
paragraphs.note: Elzon’s permanent death is established; Zol consuming him is the proposed mechanism.

sources.section: Third Age limitations and permanent death

paragraphs.text: It happened in 3A 1260 and ended the Third Age. A magical catastrophe broke over the land; the Deliverer shielded the people from it and was acclaimed the New God who had saved the world. He did not take the throne of Aenor, and a human monarchy returned. Volgan still lived in the Ember Lands.
paragraphs.note: The year and the name of the event are proposed; the rest is established.

sources.section: Third Age after the reconquest of Aenor

paragraphs.text: However great Elzon’s necromancy had been, it never gave him Zol’s rank or the right to rule death. It is not known whether the dead he raised were ever bound in soul, or only in body and memory.

plate.subject: a radiant shield over a fleeing crowd, no face

paragraphs.text: When Elzon fell in 3A 1260, his ruin brought a magical catastrophe on the lands he had ruled. The temples tell that in that hour the Deliverer stood between the people and the disaster and shielded them from it.
paragraphs.note: The year is proposed; the rescue is established.

paragraphs.text: For that rescue he was hailed as a New God, the God of Deliverance, Protection and Renewal, and the people worship him still as the Deliverer. The rescue is the heart of his worship in every temple that bears his name.
paragraphs.note: The title God of Deliverance, Protection and Renewal is proposed; his acclamation and worship are established.

paragraphs.text: He did not take the throne. A good king of men restored Aenor, and the Fourth Age began in peace. His cult keeps a feast in his honour, but no month, for the twelve months of the year honour the twelve main New Gods.

The Deliverer was Afrit, whose father was Ein, son of Aen. His help at the Last Tithe was real, and he truly shielded people from the catastrophe. It also won him what he had long prepared for: the gratitude of the people, their dependence on his temples and charities, and a place beside the restored crown from which his hidden influence grew through the long peace.

sources.section: Why the long rule holds together

paragraphs.text: The name Afrit was known chiefly to his secret council, to his enemies and to certain beings of the spirit world. Whether he was ever a true New God, of the order the Holy Seven made, is not known.
